This provides substantial, target-specific research and modelling capacity relevant to forest conservation and sustainable use, but the findings support rather than themselves carry out conservation, restoration, or sustainable-use management actions.

evidence: HIDTECH fills these gaps by pioneering a novel methodology to reconstruct these hidden technologies across Europe and the Levant, from the Upper Palaeolithic to the Early Neolithic. | Our approach integrates AI-driven quantitative use-wear analysis of durable tools (stone, bone, shell) from habitation sites and grave offerings, combined with robotic dental experiments and analysis of anterior tooth wear, revealing the use of teeth as tools. | Use-wear on tools from habitation sites will enable reconstruction of missing hide and plant technologies, while analysis of grave offerings and anterior teeth of sexed individuals (identified by proteomics) will link both hidden technologies to gendered labor roles. | By quantifying innovation rates in hide and plant-fibre technologies and correlating them with environmental, demographic, and social connectivity data, HIDTECH provides the first large-scale empirical framework for understanding factors shaping the development and transmission of these technologies.
